question: By what means does the speaker claim to have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching in address to the lord of the Kaulas?
premises: The address is made to the lord of the Kaulas.
The speaker claims to have become known or to have come to know.
That knowing is attributed to the grace of the one addressed.
The object known is the determination of the Kaula teaching.
inference: It is by the grace of the lord of the Kaulas that the speaker has come to know the Kaula determination.
uncertainties: The exact sense of jñāta in this construction remains context-dependent.
plain_english: By your grace, O lord of the Kaulas, I have come to know the determination of the Kaula teaching.
